meta.source: NYC Heat Emergency Plan as published by NYC Emergency Management and DOHMH
meta.note: New York's plan is published across NYCEM's Extreme Heat hazard page and its own press releases rather than as a single numbered PDF, so 'page' here indexes the saved source text rather than a printed page. Every quote below is verbatim from that saved text and is verified against it mechanically, exactly as the Phoenix clauses are verified against their PDF.
meta.measurement_caveat: NYC triggers on HEAT INDEX. FortyGuard's gridded products return dry-bulb air temperature. Heat index equals or exceeds air temperature whenever relative humidity is above roughly 40%, which is the normal condition for a New York summer. Evaluating these clauses against dry-bulb therefore UNDER-COUNTS the days the trigger would fire, and every divergence figure derived from them is a lower bound -- the same direction of conservatism as the citywide proxy itself.

clauses.source_text: New York City defines extreme heat events as periods when the heat index is 100°F or higher for one or more days, or 95°F or higher for two or more consecutive days.
clauses.action: Declare an extreme heat event and activate the Heat Emergency Plan: open cooling centres across the five boroughs, expand outreach to at-risk residents, and coordinate with healthcare providers and utilities.
clauses.extraction_note: Threshold and operator stated verbatim. Measured against dry-bulb daily maximum rather than heat index -- see meta.measurement_caveat; this makes the clause fire less often than it truly would, not more.

clauses.source_text: New York City defines extreme heat events as periods when the heat index is 100°F or higher for one or more days, or 95°F or higher for two or more consecutive days.
clauses.action: Declare an extreme heat event when the 95°F condition holds on two or more consecutive days, and activate the Heat Emergency Plan.
clauses.extraction_note: The document attaches a TWO-CONSECUTIVE-DAY requirement to this threshold. The evaluator tests the daily condition; consecutive runs are reported separately in the divergence output rather than folded into the per-day determination. Confidence reduced from 1.0 for that reason, not because the threshold is uncertain.

clauses.source_text: A heat index above 95°F is especially dangerous.
clauses.action: Public guidance benchmark: the level at which the City tells residents heat becomes especially dangerous.
clauses.extraction_note: A benchmark rather than an operative trigger: it carries no action and no named deadline, but it is the number the City communicates to the public.
